cards.text: This psalm prays as one big 'us,' and it opens by pushing the spotlight away: 'Not to us, O LORD, not to us.' Friend, that's the opposite of every group project at work, where everybody's fighting to get their name on the slide.

cards.question: The psalm opens with 'Not to us, O LORD, not to us.' So where does it say the glory should go?
The glory goes to the LORD's name. What reason does the psalm give?

answers.text: His people's hard work and gifts

cards.text: Then the psalm asks, 'Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?”' I don't know about you, but I hear a LITTLE side-eye in that question.

cards.question: The nations ask, 'Where is their God?' Where does the psalm say He is?
The psalm says our God is in heaven, and He does as He ___.

cards.text: Now the psalm turns to the nations' idols and looks them up and down. First up: what they're made of, and who made them.

cards.question: The nations' idols are made of silver and ___.
The psalm says those idols were made by human hands.

cards.text: Then the psalm walks through the idols' faces: mouths, eyes, ears, noses, the full set. Looks GREAT on paper.

cards.question: The nations' idols have eyes, so at least they can see.

cards.text: Not one of those parts works, same with their hands and feet, and then the psalm adds, 'they cannot even clear their throats.' Friend, I spent YEARS buried in the back of a junk drawer, and even I could clear my throat.
Then the psalm turns from the idols to the people standing in front of them. And this part is a warning.

cards.question: What does the psalm say happens to those who make these idols?
The psalm says only the idol makers become like the idols, not the people who trust in them.

cards.text: Now the psalm stops looking at idols and calls out, 'O Israel, trust in the LORD!' Then it gives the reason in one short line.

cards.question: Right after 'O Israel, trust in the LORD!' the psalm says what the LORD is. What does it call Him?

cards.text: Then it calls out two more groups with the same call to trust. And that line again: 'He is their help and shield.'

cards.question: Besides Israel, which two groups does the psalm call to trust in the LORD?

answers.text: The house of Aaron and those who fear the LORD
The kings of Judah and the prophets of Israel
The elders of the land and the judges of Israel

cards.text: Three calls in a row, TRUST HIM, TRUST HIM, TRUST HIM, and nobody's hitting snooze on THAT alarm. Now it flips to a promise: 'The LORD is mindful of us; He will bless us.'

cards.question: He will bless the house of Israel and the house of Aaron. The psalm says He will also bless those who fear the LORD, ___ and great alike.

cards.text: Then the psalm speaks a blessing straight to the listeners: 'May the LORD give you increase.' Friend, the only thing that increased in my old drawer was the dust.

cards.question: The psalm's blessing of increase is only for the listeners, not their children.
The psalm says, 'May you be blessed by the LORD,' and then it gives Him a title. What is it?

answers.text: The Maker of heaven and earth

cards.question: Then the psalm splits things up: The highest ___ belong to the LORD, but the ___ He has given to mankind.

cards.text: Then comes a quiet line: 'It is not the dead who praise the LORD, nor any who descend into silence.' That one sits still for a second, and so do I.

cards.question: The dead don't praise the LORD. So who does the psalm say will bless Him?
The psalm says we will bless the LORD for now, but not forever.

cards.text: Both now and forevermore, and then the psalm closes with one big word: 'Hallelujah!' Those idols can't even clear their throats, friend, but we get to SHOUT.

findings.problem: The question repeats 'Not to us, O LORD, not to us,' and both wrong answers (Israel's kings, Israel's priests) are part of that 'us.' The setup rules them out, so the right answer is the only one left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'pleases' is one word. Both wrong answers ('is told', 'is asked') are two-word passive phrases, so the right answer stands out by its form.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'Silver and ___' (gold, bronze or stone) asks the baker to guess a wording detail of the line. Nothing in the setup lets them reason it out. This matches the walkthrough's bad example of guessing what David is anointed with.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Card 13 says 'this part is a warning,' which rules out both wrong answers. 'They grow wise and strong' and 'They live long lives' are good outcomes, so only the right answer fits a warning.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling verses 9-11 ('Three calls in a row, TRUST HIM...') but cites only Psalm 115:12. That opening sentence is also a recap of cards already told.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
